title: fix(app-shell): drop the flow `end` node's "Output variable" field — a key `EndConfigSchema` refuses by name
body:
Fixes #9335

## What this changes

The flow node inspector's `end` group offered an **"Output variable"** text box writing
`config.outputVariable`. `EndConfigSchema` is a **strict** object whose entire key surface is
`outcome` and `message`, so the loader refuses that key **by name**. Anything an author typed in
that box therefore made the flow unloadable — `unrecognized_keys` at parse, a 422 on save — and the
form gave no way to tell which of the group's two rows had done it. The box could only ever produce
a broken document.

**The field is removed**, and nothing lenient replaces it. Commandment #0.1: the renderer does not
grow tolerance around a contract, and an `end` node terminates rather than producing a value to
bind. Declaring the key on `EndConfigSchema` would be a spec change in another lane, deliberately
not attempted here.

Also removed: the now-dead `end.outputVariable` entry in the zh-CN overlay (`FLOW_FIELD_ZH`), which
localized the descriptor that no longer exists. That removal is unobservable by construction — an
overlay entry for a field id the table does not declare is never read — so it carries no pin; it is
dead data going out with the thing it described.

## The measurement, re-run at this branch's head

Not inherited from the card. Head `55f39ee9` (this branch's base), installed `@objectstack/spec`
**17.4.0**, run from `packages/app-shell`. Accepted rows printed beside the refusals, so the
refusals are a reading and not a dead probe:

```
{"outcome":"completed"}                                  ACCEPTED
{"outcome":"completed","outputVariable":"result"}        REJECTED: Unrecognized key(s) on this end node config: `outputVariable`. …
{"outputVariable":"result"}                              REJECTED: Unrecognized key(s) on this end node config: `outputVariable`. …
{"outcome":"refused","message":"nope"}                   ACCEPTED
{"outcome":"refused"}                                    REJECTED: `outcome: 'refused'` requires a `message` …
{"outcome":"refused","outputVariable":"result"}          REJECTED: Unrecognized key(s) on this end node config: `outputVariable`. …
```

### The masking, confirmed and pinned

The last two rows differ in exactly one key, and that is the whole finding about objectui#9336.
Read back as issue codes:

```
refused + no message      => REJECTED codes=["custom"]             count=1
refused + outputVariable  => REJECTED codes=["unrecognized_keys"]  count=1
completed (lit control)   => ACCEPTED
```

An unrecognized key short-circuits `EndConfigSchema`'s `superRefine` entirely: the missing-`message`
refusal objectui#9336 shipped **never reaches the author** on any node that used the Output variable
box. So this defect was *hiding* that one. Removing the box un-hides it, and both halves of that
reading are now pinned — in the new suite, and in objectui#9336's own suite where the loss belongs.

## How the `end` group's descriptor was identified among the nine

⛔ Not by line number and ⛔ not by the placeholder string — two different groups (`end` and
`legacy_action`) carry the byte-identical spelling `{ placeholder: 'result' }`, so a text match hits
the wrong one half the time.

It was identified **structurally**, by walking `FLOW_NODE_CONFIG`'s top-level group boundaries and
attributing every occurrence to the group whose array it sits in. Before the edit:

```
  531 group=end              610 group=(comment, script preamble)
  578 group=map              634 group=script
  583 group=create_record    930 group=subflow
  598 group=get_record      1030 group=legacy_action
  605 group=http_request
```

Exactly one is in `end`. The same sweep re-run after the edit reports seven `cfg('outputVariable'…)`
rows and **no `end` entry** — every other group untouched, byte for byte. The anchor used for the
edit was a five-line context spanning the `message` descriptor's closing `showWhen`, the target row,
and the `decision:` group header that follows — asserted unique before writing.

That sweep is not just a one-off: the new suite re-derives it as a test, over
`FLOW_NODE_TYPE_OPTIONS` plus the `action` alias, and asserts the set of types still offering the key
is **non-empty** and does **not** contain `end`. A named member (`script`) is pinned too, so the
sweep cannot pass on a degenerate list.

## The objectui#9336 pin: before and after

`FlowNodeInspector.endMessage-9336.test.tsx:215` — the same line number, flipped.

**Before** — `it('leaves the \`outputVariable\` row of the same group untouched (objectui#9335 is NOT ridden)')`,
asserting the row was still **defined**, still `kind: 'text'`, still **ungated** (`showWhen`
undefined), and that a config carrying the key still failed to parse. Its author wrote it as a
separability pin, so that a future repair of objectui#9335 "has to come past this assertion on
purpose".

**After** — `it('and the \`outputVariable\` row of the same group is GONE — objectui#9335, come past on purpose')`,
asserting the row is **undefined**, with the same lookup still finding objectui#9336's own `message`
field as the lit control (so the absence is a scoped removal, not an emptied group). It keeps the
separability read, pointed forward: the removal took the refused key and nothing else. It then pins
the un-hiding that objectui#9335 was costing it — the masked parse reports no `custom` issue, and one
key away the same parse does.

It was changed deliberately, in place, with the transition recorded in the test's own comment. ⛔ Not
deleted, ⛔ not routed around.

## Migration: nothing to migrate, and nothing gets hidden

Stated rather than left implicit.

A flow carrying `config.outputVariable` on an `end` node **cannot have loaded** under the current
contract — the schema refuses it by name, so the save that would have created it returns 422 and the
load that would have read it fails. There is no population of live documents this form produced and
the runtime accepted. (Documents predating the declaration of `EndConfigSchema` may carry the key —
the refusal message says as much — but those are already unloadable today, for that key, with or
without this change. Nothing here makes them better or worse.)

What did need checking is whether the removal **hides** such a value, and it does not. Only fields
whose path is rooted at `config` own a config key; an unowned key falls through to the
**Advanced (JSON)** block, which auto-opens when non-empty. So a stored `outputVariable` on an `end`
node is still on screen, still editable, and clearing it there deletes the key. That path is pinned
end to end: render with the key stored → no typed control, Advanced shows `{"outputVariable":"result"}`
→ clear and blur → the key is gone and what remains parses clean.

⛔ No `__legacy__` render-only stub was left behind either. That treatment (`condition` on `decision`,
the retired `script` keys) exists for keys the schema **accepts** and the runtime ignores — showing
them costs nothing because the document still loads. A key the schema **refuses** is a different
animal: a control for it, even one only shown when stored, is the same defect in a quieter costume,
and Advanced already provides the do-not-hide guarantee.

## Ablation: prediction written first, then the run

**Predicted, before running**, with the new suite written but the source untouched: section 1 (the
contract, read off the installed spec) all 3 PASS because this card does not move the spec; section 2
(the descriptor) both FAIL; section 3 (the rendered inspector) both FAIL — **3 passed / 4 failed**.

**Observed**: `Tests  4 failed | 3 passed (7)`, and the four failures were exactly the four predicted,
each for the predicted reason:

```
AssertionError: the end group offers no control for a key its own contract refuses by name:
  expected { id: 'outputVariable', …(4) } to be undefined
AssertionError: and `end` is not one of them: expected [ 'create_record', 'get_record', …(6) ] to not include 'end'
AssertionError: the end inspector offers no Output variable row: expected LABEL-ELEMENT to be null
AssertionError: still no typed control for the refused key: expected LABEL-ELEMENT to be null
```

(`LABEL-ELEMENT` stands in for the rendered label node vitest prints there; the angle-bracket form
is spelled out so GitHub's body sanitizer cannot eat it.)

The second failure is itself the lit control for the sweep: it prints the eight types that offered
the key before the edit, with `end` among them.

**On-disk proof of the mutation** (⛔ not an editor exit code): `cfg('outputVariable'…)` occurrences
in `flow-node-config.ts` went 8 → 7, and the file's blob hash moved
`4ea15bf4f6cd51087ef442e63da6ea4a2acfc3c1` → `792cc691c06b5e3bc8d4a0627533ebe2ae4f6ac9`. No mutation
was left in the tree: this is a removal, not a temporary variation, so the "restore" is the commit
itself and `git status` is clean at `433bb25`.

After the edit the new suite is **7 passed**, and objectui#9336's suite went red on exactly its
separability pin — which is the assertion this card then came past on purpose.

## Tests

All run from the repo root with path filters, through the container's shared heavy-verify lock.
Verdict lines quoted from each tool, ⛔ not a bare shell status. Measured at `433bb25`.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `FlowNodeInspector.endOutputVariable-9335.test.tsx` + `…endMessage-9336.test.tsx` | `Test Files 2 passed (2)` · `Tests 17 passed (17)` · `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/` | `Test Files 77 passed (77)` · `Tests 918 passed / 1 skipped (919)` · `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/` + `external/` | `Test Files 59 passed (59)` · `Tests 669 passed (669)` · `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the four edited files | `files linted: 4` · `errors: 0 warnings: 0` · exit 0 |
| narrowed `tsc -p` over both edited/new test files (see below) | `TSC_EXIT_A=0` · `error lines: 0`, with a lit control proving the program can red |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅ 3 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)` |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test …` | `✅ NOT GOVERNED — 5 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` |
| control-character scan (`grep -naP` over every edited file) | no matches |

### Declared narrowings

Two, both stated rather than quietly skipped.

**1. `@object-ui/app-shell`'s own `type-check` is NOT MEASURED here, and a narrowed substitute was run
instead.** `type-check` is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; both halves resolve `@object-ui/*`
through the workspace dependencies' built `.d.ts`, so they need `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`
first — a 29-package closure. Run against an unbuilt tree, `tsc --noEmit` returns a wall of TS2307
"Cannot find module `@object-ui/…`" that is a **precondition not met**, ⛔ not a red gate, so it is not
reported as one. The closure build never got a turn on the container's shared heavy-verify lock:
`VERDICT queue-timeout (exit 99) · never acquired · waited 540s (9m00s)`, the holder being a sibling
seat's `pnpm test --shard=3/4`. CI's `Type Check` job runs this properly, after `^build`.

Rather than report nothing, the check was **narrowed until it no longer needed the lock**: a throwaway
`tsc -p` project including exactly the two test files this PR adds and edits, with `@object-ui/*` mapped
to package **sources** instead of `dist` (the repo root's own `paths` block, extended to the packages it
does not already list). Result: **0 errors, exit 0**.

That zero is a reading and not a dead probe, because it is paired with a lit control. A provably-false
assertion — `const __ablationProbe: number = endFields();` — was appended to the new test file, and the
mutation was proven to have reached disk before anything was read from it (anchor grep 0 → 2; blob hash
`807871f5…` → `5b564e78…`, ⛔ not an editor exit code). The same program then reported exactly one error,
at exactly that file:

```
…/FlowNodeInspector.endOutputVariable-9335.test.tsx(286,7): error TS2322: Type 'FlowConfigField[]' is not assignable to type 'number'.
```

The restore was proven **by state**, ⛔ not by re-running anything: blob hash back to `807871f5…`
(identical to `git rev-parse HEAD:THAT-PATH`), `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` empty. The throwaway
project file was deleted in the same step and is not in the diff. ⚠️ The deviation this narrowing carries,
stated so the reading is not over-read: source resolution is not `dist` resolution, so it does not
substitute for CI's job — it answers "do the files this PR adds type-check", not "does the package".

**2.** The remaining 124 top-level `metadata-admin` test files were started and then
**stopped, so that family is NOT MEASURED here** — it was still in module transform after eleven
minutes on a three-agent container and was starving a sibling seat that had been queued on the shared
lock for over seven. It is outside this diff's blast radius: `flow-node-config.ts` is imported only by
`ExpressionProvider`, `previews/flow-expr-problems`, `i18n.ts` and the `inspectors/` tree, all of which
are covered above; the `i18n.ts` edit removes one property from a `Record`-typed literal and adds a
comment. CI runs the farm.

## Clause-②: no

Re-declared after the diff, not predicted from it. `flow-node-config.ts` is not exported from
`packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`, and every importer of it is internal to `@object-ui/app-shell`
(enumerated above). No exported type, no published `exports` entry and no wire shape moved. The only
accept set that moved is the set of keys this **form** can produce, and it shrank — toward the
contract, by exactly the one key the runtime already refused. So no `needs:contract-review`.

## Acceptance notes

Observations found in passing, recorded here rather than filed — each named with who would meet it:

- `FlowNodeInspector.specKeys.test.tsx` closes the **node-level** refused-key class
  (`SPEC_REFUSED_NODE_KEYS` is `['description']`, and `withoutSpecRefusedKeys` strips node keys only).
  Nothing in this repo does the same for **config** keys against each node type's discriminated config
  schema, which is why this defect and objectui#9278 were both found by hand rather than by CI.
  `scripts/check-designer-field-key-parity.mjs` covers field / object / permission designer payloads,
  so the flow-node config table is out of its field of view. Noted, not filed: this is a gate-coverage
  proposal, not a reproducible defect, and the card already records it. Who would meet it: the next
  seat that repairs a third row of this table.
- `FLOW_FIELD_ZH` has no parity gate against `FLOW_NODE_CONFIG` — an overlay entry for a field id the
  table does not declare is silently ignored, which is exactly how `end.outputVariable` would have
  survived this removal unnoticed. Noted, not filed: no runtime consequence (dead data, never read),
  and a gate for it is the same proposal as the row above. Who would meet it: anyone removing or
  renaming a flow config field id.
